name: Lord Cromer (Evelyn Baring)

summary.text: Lord Cromer is the title of Evelyn Baring, British commissioner on Egypt's Caisse de la Dette from 1877 and British agent and consul-general in Egypt 1883-1907. See the file for evelyn-baring; this entry records the same person under the title used on the Crash Conduits page.

sources.publisher: Reviews in History (Institute of Historical Research)
sources.title: Review of Roger Owen, Lord Cromer: Victorian Imperialist, Edwardian Proconsul

facts.claim: He served as British agent and consul-general in Egypt from 1883 to 1907, having been financial member of the Viceroy's council in India from 1880 to 1883.
facts.quote: He remained there till 1883, and was then appointed British agent and consul-general in Egypt.

facts.claim: He was raised to the peerage as Baron Cromer in 1892 and became Earl of Cromer in 1901; he died in London on 29 January 1917.
Roger Owen's biography, as reviewed, describes Cromer as the effective ruler of Egypt from 1883 to 1907 while formally only consul-general, backed by British troops and some 400 British officials.

connections.claim: Lord Cromer and Evelyn Baring are the same person.

openQuestions: Evelyn Baring and Lord Cromer are the same person (Evelyn Baring, 1st Earl of Cromer); the site lists them as two entities.
Site claim tested: 'British commissioner of the Caisse de la Dette 1877-79' is supported in substance; sources differ on whether he was Controller-General in 1878-79 or 1879-80.
Site claim tested: 'ran Egyptian finances 1883-1907' is consistent with the biographical sources' description of his consul-generalship.
